content.value_statement: Agent identity data can be difficult to inspect across blockchain registries. This skill resolves ERC-8004 records and prepares AgentCards without sending transactions.
actual_capabilities: Resolve an ERC-8004 agent ID to its owner and decoded AgentCard.
Handle data, HTTPS, and IPFS tokenURI forms during agent resolution.
List canonical Identity and Reputation Registry addresses by chain.
Generate a registration-v1 AgentCard with services and trust models.
Include optional x402 support in a generated AgentCard.
Keep provided workflows read-only or scaffolding-only.
limitations: It does not register agents or submit reputation feedback on-chain.
ERC-8004 write interfaces may change while specification work continues.
Public RPC fallback reliability depends on network availability.
Generated AgentCards require separate hosting and registration steps.

best_practices: Verify resolved ownership and endpoints before trusting an agent service.
Host generated AgentCards at stable public URLs before registration.
Use approved reference contracts for every on-chain write operation.
anti_patterns: Do not treat AgentCard claims as proof of service safety or quality.
Do not submit generated metadata through unverified write interfaces.
Do not rely on public RPC fallback for production-critical availability.

faq.question: Does this skill send blockchain transactions?
faq.answer: No. It supports read-only resolution and AgentCard scaffolding only.

faq.question: What is ERC-8004?
faq.answer: ERC-8004 is a draft standard for portable on-chain AI agent identity and reputation.

faq.question: What information can agent resolution return?
faq.answer: It can return agent ownership and a decoded AgentCard from the registered tokenURI.

faq.question: Can it create an AgentCard?
faq.answer: Yes. It generates registration-v1 AgentCard metadata with services, trust models, and optional x402 support.

faq.question: Does generated metadata register an agent?
faq.answer: No. You must host the metadata and register through approved contracts after write interfaces are final.

faq.question: Why set BASE_RPC_URL?
faq.answer: A configured RPC endpoint can improve reliability when public RPC fallback endpoints are unavailable.
